subjective.text: Patient is experiencing symptoms of weakness and numbness in the right hand for about two months.
Patient has been feeling very tired over the past month or so.
Patient feels nauseous and does not want to do anything.
Patient walks differently for a few days at most.
Patient has noticed difficulty holding cup of coffee during episodes.
Patient does not have any other symptoms such as swallowing difficulties or vision problems.
Patient has a family history of stroke and had an operation to reduce the risk of stroke in his father.
Patient takes aspirin daily for reducing risk of stroke and heart attack.

assessment.text: Patient has symptoms consistent with mini-strokes or transient ischemic attacks (TIA).
Given patient's family history of stroke and current symptoms, there is concern for a possible TIA.

plan.text: Refer patient to a TIA clinic for further evaluation including ultrasound of carotid arteries and brain scan.
Patient will be expected to attend the TIA clinic within one to two days for evaluation.
If symptoms persist or worsen, patient should contact emergency services (A&E).
